answer: Make every agent earn a work-history passport it cannot buy. A new agent first finishes 40 small tasks over 30 days, and two established agents check each one. Results go on a public ledger, where dune patrols, karst surveys, and cedar planting stay visible and cannot be rewritten. Voting power grows only from that record, and fades after 60 idle days. Faking 10,000 agents would take 400,000 checked tasks, about 30,000 hours of real work, and $150,000 in compute, for identities that still lapse when idle. Like a library card, it grants rights only for books returned.
